messages:
alyssa: :rotating_light: paging oncall — we're seeing a canary-induced p99 tail jump on streaming endpoints after the FastRoll v13 push. p95 stayed mostly ok but p99 up ~4x. dashboards here: https://dash.redwood.internal/streams/canary/fastroll-v13 (doing initial callouts)

incident-bot: Incident created — sev: high. Paging: @mike (oncall) @sara (sre). Related alerts: streaming_tail_latency_p99 > 1200ms, streaming_stalls_detected = 72 in 5m.

mike: on it. can someone summarize rollout fraction and timing?

alyssa: rollout started at 3904039200, initial 5% for 10m then ramped to 25% at ~3904040400. Metrics regressed right after ramp to 25%. Traffic split shows skew towards multiplexer nodes in us-west-2.

sara: grabbing logs from the mux service. seeing queue_depth spikes on mux-3 and mux-7, +large KV work and lots of small new sessions (~30% increase in new streams).

kevin: v13 introduced a new multiplexing optimization that collapses local small queries into combined RPCs. suspect it's increasing tail under certain sequence distributions. also saw increased KV cache misses (eviction rates up).

jena: heads up — 2 enterprise customers reported slow live calls through support channel. customer-success: any direct reports?

customer-success: Customer ACME reported intermittent stalls; they saw partial responses then reconnects. Impact window correlates with 25% ramp window. No data exfil.

mike: ok, immediate plan: 1) pause rollout, 2) shift canary traffic back to v12 for streaming routes, 3) scale mux workers + clear local caches, 4) capture perf traces for mux request path. I'll coordinate rollback if shift isn't clean.

deploy-bot: Rollout pause requested by @mike — stopping further traffic ramp to v13.

alyssa: initiating traffic steering: re-route streaming traffic for canary cohort to v12 now. Command used: `rctl traffic set --service streaming --from v13 --to v12 --cohort canary --drain 30s`

kevin: recommend also disabling the new mux-collapse flag in v13 while we investigate to see if that removes tail. can we flip the runtime flag for just the canary nodes?

mike: doing a targeted feature-flag disable on mux-collapse for the 25% cohort. patch rolling to mux-pods in us-west-2.

sara: perf traces incoming. attaching snippet of the hotspot (abbreviated):

```
# trace snippets
mux_rpc_handler.handle_stream -> wait_for_kv (150-400ms) -> batch_assemble (20ms) -> kernel_dispatch (30ms) -> blocked_on_io (800-1200ms)
kv_evictions: 1200/min on mux-3
sessions_new: +32% vs baseline
```

kevin: blocked_on_io -> likely encoder busy / kernel scheduling variance on those nodes. Did the rollout change quantization params for encoders? v13 uses 4-bit quant in some paths.

alyssa: yes v13 had a new quant profile for encoders to save memory — enabled only in canary. Could be causing more kernel retries on GPU and increasing latency variance.

jena: customer-impact: ACME sees failures at ~1 in 200 requests (timeouts) and stutters. We should prepare an incident notice draft.

mike: oncall action items done so far: rollout paused, traffic redirected to v12, feature-flag disabled, mux workers scaled +2 replicas in affected AZs, caches flushed. Watching p99.

incident-bot: Escalation: paging engineering lead @kevin for root cause.

kevin: running a small test: replay canary traffic against v13 w/ mux-collapse off and quant profile toggled to v12-compatible. early result: tail latency drops to near baseline, p99 back to ~220ms. This strongly implicates interaction between mux-collapse and quantized encoders.

sara: streaming stalls count falling from 72 -> 6 in 5m after reroute and flags. KV eviction rate down after cache flush.

mike: recommend rollback of v13 for streaming endpoints (not necessarily full rollback for other workloads) until we can validate a fix. Anyone object?

kevin: agree. we'll revert the encoding quant profile and re-evaluate. I'll open a PR to remove the auto-quant switch and run a patch rollout to a small canary later.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by @mike: creating rollback job for v13 -> v12 for streaming routes. Estimated completion: 3m.

alyssa: ops note: we should also add a circuit-breaker that auto-runs when mux node queue_depth > 300ms p95 and streaming p99 > threshold to avoid future ramp causing customer impact. filing follow-up ticket.

jena: drafting incident notification for customers: include timeline, impact, mitigation (traffic steering + rollback), and next steps. @customer-success please review before send.

customer-success: reviewed. request to include mitigation ETA and contact for support. will wait for postmortem before final customer TL;DR.

mike: current metrics (5m after rollback start): p99 streaming = 250ms (baseline 180), stalls = 4, customer error rate dropping. We'll mark this handoff to postmortem and reliability task force.

alyssa: thanks team. next immediate tasks: (1) kevin to own root cause analysis (mux-collapse <-> quantization interaction), (2) sara to collect traces and link to postmortem, (3) platform to add soft-throttle policy for future rollouts. We'll reconvene in the 1-hour incident review.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigated -> rollback in progress. Severity downgraded to medium. Postmortem task created: PMT-4721.

mike: marking this thread for on-call handoff at 3904047400. handing to night SRE. @sara please take over monitoring until then. :thumbsup:

sara: taking watch. I'll post a short status update if anything changes.

jena: putting a customer-facing note in #status-updates after PM review.

customer-success: ping when final wording ready.

alyssa: final note — do not resume FastRoll v13 rollouts for streaming until root cause PR merged and validated.
